citations.title: Residential care facility definitions
citations.requirement: Defines an RCF in two prongs: 17+ unrelated residents with personal care for 3+, or 3+ residents with personal care for 3+ and skilled nursing for 1+. Also defines skilled nursing care and the resident call system (par. FF).

citations.title: General provisions and prohibitions
citations.requirement: An RCF may not admit or retain residents who need skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011 limits. Par. (D) sets the services an RCF may provide, and 3701-16-07(A) bars admission beyond it.

citations.title: Initial, renewal and change of operator license applications
citations.requirement: Initial application due at least 60 days before opening. Needs CPA-signed 3-month solvency statement, certificate of occupancy (R-4, I-1 or I-2), fire and heating reports. Renewal needs application and fee. Change of operator due 60 days ahead.

citations.title: Procedures for inspecting and licensing homes; fees
citations.requirement: Non-refundable fee of $320 per 50 beds or part thereof. ODH inspects at least every 15 months (30 months if clean-record conditions are met). Fire marshal or approved fire department inspects at least every 15 months.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: administrator
citations.requirement: Administrator is responsible for daily operation and must provide at least 20 hours per week on site between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. An acting administrator (21+) is designated for absences. Administrator must be reachable at other times.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staff on duty and on call
citations.requirement: At least one qualified personal care staff member on duty at all times. The overnight person may be on call only if call system rules in 3701-16-14(B)(5) are met. When only one person is on duty, designate another qualified staff member on call.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: sufficient staff, evacuation, first aid
citations.requirement: Staff enough to meet assessed care, supervision and emotional needs, dietary, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and activities. Staff needed for the evacuation plan are present at all times. A first-aid-trained personal care staff member is on site at all times.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staffing basis and clinical consultant
citations.requirement: Staffing need not count needs met by third parties or refused by the resident, if documented. A facility admitting late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs or serious mental illness residents must have a psychologist or physician on staff or consulting.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: RN supervision of skilled nursing
citations.requirement: A facility providing skilled nursing beyond special diets, dressings or medication must employ or contract an RN for onsite supervision, have a licensed nurse on call, and have enough nursing staff.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: coverage schedule; residents not to work
citations.requirement: Operator or administrator sets a coverage schedule that includes vacations, emergencies and long absences. Residents may not be mandated, coerced or persuaded to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: medication, diet, dressing and skilled-care staffing
citations.requirement: A facility that administers medication needs an RN, a medication-course LPN (acting at an RN or physician direction), a physician, or another person authorized by law on duty. Dietitian needed for therapeutic diets. Enough nurses for dressings or skilled care.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staffing records; admission limit
citations.requirement: Keep personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms. Do not admit more residents than the facility can serve with consistent nursing coverage and other appropriate staffing for resident volume and needs.

citations.title: Personnel health: communicable disease, impairment, pre-employment exam
citations.requirement: Staff with a transmissible disease may not work while communicable unless duties are modified. Staff may not be impaired by alcohol or drugs. Every paid worker is examined within 30 days before starting or on day one. Retain exam copies.

citations.title: Staff age and language requirements
citations.requirement: Personal care staff are 16+ (under 18 need on-site supervision by an adult over 18). Administrator is 21+. Staff assisting with medication must read, write and understand English. Activity planners need training for cognitive and mental illness populations.

citations.title: Personal care staff: first aid and competency
citations.requirement: First-aid training within 60 days of hire (Red Cross, AHA, or equivalent). Before working unsupervised, staff must complete RN or LPN-taught personal care training, an ODH-approved aide program, or Medicare home health aide training.

citations.title: Special-population training, annual CE and therapeutic diet training
citations.requirement: Cognitive impairment and serious mental illness care: 2 hrs initial within 14 days and 4 hrs CE yearly (4 and 8 hrs if both groups are served). All personal care staff: 8 hrs CE yearly. Dietitian training before therapeutic diets.

citations.title: Administrator qualifications and continuing education
citations.requirement: Administrator holds a nursing home administrator license, or has 3,000 hours of operational responsibility, 100 credit hours in gerontology or health care, a bachelor's degree, or a licensed health professional credential. 9 hrs CE yearly.

citations.title: Orientation within three working days
citations.requirement: Each staff member completes orientation within 3 working days: physical layout, job duties, policies and procedures, how to secure emergency help, and resident rights. No staff member is alone with residents until orientation and fire training are complete.

citations.title: Professional licensure and annual resident-rights training
citations.requirement: Professionals used by the facility hold current Ohio licenses where required. Annual (calendar-year) staff training on each ORC 3721.13(A) right and on comparable service for residents with similar needs, plus as needed.

citations.title: Disqualifications for direct-care employment
citations.requirement: Do not employ in direct care anyone with a disqualifying offense under ORC 3721.121(C)(1), who fails forms or fingerprints, or who has an abuse, neglect or misappropriation finding on the Ohio or another state's nurse aide registry or a license action for the same.

citations.title: Admission prohibitions and sex offender search
citations.requirement: Search the Ohio sex offender registry before admission. Do not admit or retain (except hospice) residents needing skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011, 8+ hrs/day or 40+ hrs/week, restraints, bedridden, stage III/IV pressure ulcers, or unstable conditions.

citations.title: Written resident agreement
citations.requirement: Signed, dated agreement before residency, with a copy and explanation provided. It covers charges and deposits, 30-day written notice of a rate change, refund policy, services, skilled nursing limits and mandatory discharge if limits are exceeded.

citations.title: Pre-admission policy disclosures and risk agreements
citations.requirement: Before admission, give and explain the rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR (not a condition of admission), disability accommodation and special care unit policies. Written risk agreements need the resident's consent and a signed acknowledgment; rights waivers are void.

citations.title: Initial resident health assessment
citations.requirement: Written assessment within 48 hours of admission (items (C)(11)-(12) within 14 days). An assessment done within 90 days before admission may be used. Covers preferences, diagnoses, falls risk, medications, diet, function and self-administration. Offer flu and pneumococcal vaccines yearly.

citations.title: Annual reassessment and change in condition
citations.requirement: Reassess health at least annually, within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner when a change in condition or function warrants new services or equipment. Document diagnoses, diet, weight, medications and function.

citations.title: Special care unit placement; unmet needs; transfer or discharge
citations.requirement: Secured special care unit admission requires a licensed professional's determination, an updated agreement, and cannot rest on diagnosis alone. If needs exceed services, hold a resident meeting, discuss waiver options, and discharge under ORC 3721.16 and OAC Ch. 3701-61 if needed.

citations.title: Personal care services
citations.requirement: State the extent and types of personal care in policies and agreements and provide it to residents who need it, unless refused or covered by a risk agreement. Care must meet accepted standards, be given by trained staff, and match the assessment.

citations.title: Medication self-administration and administration
citations.requirement: Medications are self-administered except as authorized. Staff may only remind, hand over, open containers or assist physically impaired residents; they may not fill pill organizers. Administration is limited to an RN, a qualified LPN, a physician, or another authorized person, on a prescriber's order.

citations.title: Medication orders, storage, labeling, records, disposal
citations.requirement: Telephone orders go to a licensed nurse only and are signed within 14 days. Keep all prescription drugs locked. Do not repackage or relabel. Keep a medication list and administration record. Send medications with the resident or destroy them with consent. Prevent controlled-substance theft.

citations.title: Application of dressings
citations.requirement: A facility that provides dressings must write down which dressings it manages, have written procedures, use only authorized individuals, evaluate each such resident at least every 7 days for transfer, document in the record, and have a nurse coordinate care.

citations.title: Prohibition on restraints and isolation
citations.requirement: Physical, chemical and isolation restraints are forbidden (includes locked room doors and geriatric chairs). Secured special care units are allowed only if individualized, reviewed at each reassessment, code compliant, and not based solely on diagnosis.

citations.title: Skilled nursing: 120-day limit and extended-care agreement
citations.requirement: Part-time intermittent skilled nursing is capped at 120 days per 12 months. Beyond that, a written agreement with the resident and physician is required, with re-determination at least every 30 days (hospice: every 15 days).

citations.title: Skilled nursing by facility staff; enteral feedings
citations.requirement: Written procedures, authorized providers only, evaluation at least every 7 days for transfer, orders signed within 14 days, and a coordinating nurse. Part-time intermittent enteral feedings also require written types, weight documentation and a dietitian.

citations.title: Dietary services; supervision of therapeutic diets
citations.requirement: Specify meals offered (0-3 daily). Max 16 hours between supper and breakfast, evening snack, menus planned a week ahead and kept 3 months, a week of staples and 2 days of perishables, always-available drinking water, and a dietitian for therapeutic diets.

citations.title: Activities, pets and laundry
citations.requirement: Provide or arrange varied activities (daily newspaper or community brochures, community activity and transport information). Written pet protocol after a veterinarian consult. Specify laundry services in the resident agreement.

citations.title: Resident finances and guardianship
citations.requirement: Do not coerce assignment of assets. Managing funds needs a witnessed written authorization. Funds over $1,000 go in a separate interest-bearing account, with a surety bond and a final accounting. Staff may not be guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related.

citations.title: Change in health status and incidents
citations.requirement: On a significant adverse change, get immediate intervention, note it in the record, give information to the treating party, and notify the sponsor. For incidents, investigate and keep a separate incident log with time, place, date, description and action.

citations.title: Infection prevention and control; TB plan; water management
citations.requirement: Written infection program with a trained designee reported to ODH within 10 days of any change, a TB control plan (3701-15-03), a surveillance plan, isolation, hand hygiene and laundry rules, and a legionella water management program.

citations.title: Building, plumbing, egress and electrical safety
citations.requirement: Certificate of occupancy, Ohio plumbing code, thermostatic mixing devices on bathing fixtures, Ohio fire code compliance, clear egress, door hold-opens only if they release on power loss or alarm, and safe electrical systems and appliances.

citations.title: Written disaster preparedness plan
citations.requirement: Written plan, kept on site and electronically off-site. Covers evacuation (impaired mobility, transport to receiving facilities), fire watch, missing residents with law enforcement notification, severe weather, and telling ODH of any business interruption.

citations.title: Fire and disaster drills and records
citations.requirement: 12 fire drills a year (one per shift every 3 months), each staff member in one a year, residents evacuated in 2 drills per shift yearly, 2 disaster drills yearly (one tornado drill March-July). Keep written records 3 years.

citations.title: Evacuation maps, systems, fire training, monthly inspection
citations.requirement: Post floor plans on each floor. Automatic sprinklers and fire alarms, with records kept. Fire and evacuation training within 3 working days, annual fire prevention training, resident emergency training, monthly fire safety inspection (kept 3 years), and CO detectors.

citations.title: Smoking and oxygen safety
citations.requirement: Smoking and vaping only in designated areas. No smoking or flame where oxygen is stored or used, with signs posted. Take reasonable precautions for smoking residents, use non-combustible ash receptacles, and provide shelter in bad weather.

citations.title: Fire reporting and transfer agreements
citations.requirement: Report any fire, fire damage, or fire or smoke illness, injury or death to the State Fire Marshal and ODH within 24 hours on their forms. Keep written transfer agreements with facilities that can meet residents' needs.

citations.title: Space requirements
citations.requirement: New units: 100 sq ft single, 80 sq ft per person shared, max 4 per room. Resident-activated call system in rooms and bathrooms. One toilet, sink and tub or shower per 8 residents. Hot water 105-120 F where facility controlled.

citations.title: Residents' rights: care, dignity, privacy, restraints, communication
citations.requirement: Rights include freedom from abuse, informed consent, record confidentiality, privacy, freedom from restraint except by physician order (12-hour emergency limit), choice of pharmacist and physician, unrestricted communication, and civil rights. Waiver is void ((C)).

citations.title: Residents' rights: charges, finances, property, room changes
citations.requirement: Written notice of basic rate and extra charges; 30 days' notice of rate change; itemized monthly bill; freedom from financial exploitation; quarterly accounting if funds are delegated; access to deposited property; notice before room or roommate change.

citations.title: Residents' rights: transfer and discharge; hospice choice
citations.requirement: Discharge allowed only for listed reasons (needs unmet, improved, safety, nonpayment, license loss, etc.). Needs adequate preparation and a destination that can meet needs. The resident may choose a licensed hospice.

citations.title: Residents' rights: grievances and sponsor notice
citations.requirement: Residents may voice grievances to staff, ODH or others of their choice without reprisal, including access to a residents' rights advocate. Make a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of a significant health change within 12 hours.

citations.title: Criminal records checks for direct-care applicants
citations.requirement: Referenced by OAC 3701-16-06(L): forms and fingerprints are required (division (B)(2)), and offenses in division (C)(1) disqualify. Statute text not fetched in this pass; read before drafting procedures.

citations.title: Transfer and discharge procedures
citations.requirement: Referenced by OAC 3701-16-08(G)(3) and 3701-16-09(C) as governing required transfers and discharges. Notice periods and content not fetched in this pass; confirm before drafting.

citations.title: Tuberculosis control plan standards
citations.requirement: Referenced by OAC 3701-16-12(C)(2): the RCF TB control plan must meet these standards. Content, including employee screening, not fetched in this pass.

citations.title: Fire inspection of residential care facilities
citations.requirement: Referenced by OAC 3701-16-13(H) as governing fire safety inspections of the RCF. Text not fetched in this pass.

citations.title: HCBS waivers: assisted living
citations.requirement: Governs administration and reimbursement of the Assisted Living Waiver. Residents must live in an ODH-licensed RCF, and the maximum rates are in Appendix A. Services only, not room and board.

citations.title: Assisted living HCBS waiver program
citations.requirement: Assisted Living Waiver provider rules: ODH-licensed RCF plus ODA waiver provider certification, and a three-tier unit rate model. Individual rule text not fetched in this pass.

citations.title: HCBS waiver setting requirements
citations.requirement: HCBS setting requirements for waiver residents: choice, privacy, dignity, freedom from coercion, and control of schedule and visitors. Text not fetched in this pass.

citations.title: HIPAA privacy administrative requirements
citations.requirement: Covered-entity privacy duties: privacy official, workforce training, safeguards, complaint process, and sanctions. Applies if the facility is a covered entity (e.g., it bills Medicaid electronically). Text not fetched in this pass.

citations.title: OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard
citations.requirement: Exposure control plan, training, PPE, and hepatitis B vaccine offer for employees with occupational exposure. Text not fetched in this pass.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: Administrator runs daily operation and is on site at least 20 hours per week between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.
Designate an acting administrator (age 21+) for absences; the administrator must be reachable at other times
Operator or administrator sets a written coverage schedule covering vacations, emergencies and long absences
Residents may not be mandated, coerced or persuaded to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: Initial application is filed at least 60 days before the proposed opening, with a CPA-signed 3-month solvency statement
License fee is $320 per 50 beds or part thereof, non-refundable, due with the initial and renewal applications
ODH inspects at least every 15 months (30 months if clean-record conditions are met); the fire marshal or approved fire department inspects at least every 15 months
One license per building, except buildings on the same lot operated as one facility
ODH Licensure Unit: liccert@odh.ohio.gov, (614) 466-7713; cite OAC Ch. 3701-16, never 3701-17 (nursing homes)

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Review all policies at least annually and whenever OAC Ch. 3701-16 or ORC 3721 changes
Policies given to residents before admission (rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR, special care unit, disability accommodation) must be current and version-controlled
Staff sign an acknowledgment of policy changes; annual rights training uses the current policy
Keep a citation index mapping each policy to its OAC/ORC section

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Quarterly internal audit against OAC Ch. 3701-16 (facility standard; the survey cycle is 9-15 months, unannounced)
Review the incident log, infection surveillance data and drill evaluations for trends
Drill problems must be investigated and corrected, with written evaluation kept 3 years
Governing body reviews QA results and corrective actions at least quarterly

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Applies to Assisted Living Waiver billing; the waiver pays for services, not room and board
ODM provider enrollment is electronic only; $750 organizational application fee unless waived with proof of payment within 2 years
Respond to ODM revalidation notices (sent at least 90 days before the deadline); keep contact details current
Whether EVV applies to Assisted Living Waiver claims is unconfirmed; obtain written confirmation from ODA/ODM
Billing codes, unit definitions and Appendix A rates come from ODA/ODM; do not bill from unverified rates

policies.title: Closure, Change of Operator and Resident Relocation Plan
state_specifics: Closure notice to the ODH director at least 90 days ahead where practicable, and no less than 60 days

Notice must state an address where the operator can be reached, a plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and assurances that residents go to the most integrated and appropriate setting considering needs, choice and best interests
Change-of-operator application is due at least 60 days before the proposed assignment or transfer, with a non-refundable fee
Resident discharge and transfer notices follow ORC 3721.16 and OAC Ch. 3701-61 (notice periods not verified; confirm before drafting)

policies.title: Assisted Living Waiver Provider Participation and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Waiver residents must live in an ODH-licensed RCF; the facility also needs ODA waiver provider certification
Administered by ODA under an interagency agreement with ODM; maximum rates are in Appendix A to OAC 5160-1-06.5
Three-tier unit rate model; confirm memory care tier certification and critical access criteria with ODA in writing
Honor HCBS setting rights: choice, privacy, dignity, freedom from coercion, control of schedule and visitors
Keep a written waiver waitlist policy (first-come); verify slot availability with ODA

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Give and explain the ORC 3721.12/3721.13 rights policy and procedures before admission
Rights include freedom from abuse, informed consent, privacy, record confidentiality, choice of physician and pharmacist, and unrestricted communication
Waiver of rights is void; risk agreements may not waive them
Annual (calendar-year) staff training on each ORC 3721.13(A) right and on comparable service for residents with similar needs
Reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of a significant health change within 12 hours

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Residents may voice grievances to staff, ODH or others of their choice without reprisal
Give access to a residents' rights advocate
Written grievance procedure with a log, investigation and written response
Post ODH complaint hotline and Ohio LTC Ombudsman numbers as currently published (verify before posting)

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Residents' right to communicate unrestricted with a residents' rights advocate or ombudsman
Staff may not interfere with, screen or retaliate for ombudsman contact
Post ombudsman contact information where residents can see it (verify current numbers)
Give ombudsman representatives access to residents and, with consent, to records

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Signed, dated agreement before residency, with a copy and explanation given to the resident or sponsor
Must explain all charges and deposits and state that all charges, fines or penalties assessed against the resident are included
Basic rate may not change without 30 days' written notice to the resident, or to the sponsor if the resident cannot understand it
Must explain the refund policy for absence, discharge or transfer and for security deposits, and who pays for services
Must describe services, skilled nursing types allowed, providers and limits, and state that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing beyond those limits

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Managing resident funds requires a witnessed written authorization
Funds over $1,000 go in a separate interest-bearing account, with a surety bond and a final accounting
Quarterly accounting if funds are delegated; itemized monthly bill
Staff may not be guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related; no coercion to assign assets
Residents keep access to deposited property

policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Give the advance directive and DNR policy, with an explanation of resident rights under state law, before admission
An advance directive or DNR order may not be required as a condition of admission
Copy of any directive or DNR is kept in the record and honored per the policy
Have counsel confirm the staff response procedure (statutory cites not verified here)

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Record confidentiality and privacy are resident rights under ORC 3721.13(A)
HIPAA duties apply if the facility is a covered entity (e.g., bills Medicaid electronically)
If covered: designate a privacy official, train the workforce, set safeguards, a complaint process and sanctions
Release records only with resident or sponsor authorization or as law requires

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Civil rights are protected under ORC 3721.13(A)
Give each prospective resident an explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabilities and its policy for transfers to accommodating units
Provide interpreter or translated materials for limited-English residents
Staff who assist with medication must read, write and understand English

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Search the Ohio sex offender registry before admission and keep the result
Do not admit residents who need skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011 limits, 8+ hours/day or 40+ hours/week
Do not admit or retain residents who need restraints, are bedridden, have stage III/IV pressure ulcers or have unstable conditions (hospice excepted)
Do not admit more residents than staffing can serve with consistent nursing coverage

policies.title: Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet
state_specifics: Give and explain before admission: rights policy, smoking policy, advance directive/DNR policy
Include the OAC 3701-16-01 definition of skilled nursing care
Include the disability accommodation explanation and the policy on transfers to accommodating units
Include any other facility policies residents must follow; keep a signed acknowledgment
Rule -07(F)(2) cites 3701-16-13(W) for smoking; the smoking content is at 3701-16-13(U)

policies.title: Risk Agreements
state_specifics: If the facility enters risk agreements, give each prospective resident or sponsor a written explanation of the policy and the provisions an agreement may contain
Keep a signed acknowledgment on file
Each risk agreement needs the resident's consent and a signed acknowledgment
Rights waivers are void; a risk agreement may not waive rights
Care covered by a risk agreement is documented in the service plan

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Written initial assessment within 48 hours of admission (items (C)(11)-(12) within 14 days)
An assessment done within 90 days before admission may be used
Covers preferences, diagnoses, falls risk, medications, diet, function and self-administration
Reassess at least annually within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner on a change in condition
Offer influenza and pneumococcal vaccines yearly

policies.title: Service / Care Plan
state_specifics: State the extent and types of personal care in policies and the agreement
Provide care to residents who need it unless refused or covered by a risk agreement
Care meets accepted standards, is given by trained staff and matches the assessment
Document needs met by third parties or refused by the resident
Update the plan at each reassessment and on change in condition

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Skilled nursing care is defined in OAC 3701-16-01 and given to residents before admission
Part-time intermittent skilled nursing is capped at 120 days per 12 months
Beyond 120 days: written agreement with resident and physician, re-determination at least every 30 days (hospice every 15)
Do not retain residents needing skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011 limits (hospice excepted)
The facility must discharge or transfer a resident who exceeds the limits stated in the agreement

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Discharge only for reasons listed in ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33)
Needs adequate preparation and a destination that can meet the resident's needs
If needs exceed services, hold a resident meeting and discuss waiver options before discharge
Follow ORC 3721.16 and OAC Ch. 3701-61 for notice (periods not verified; confirm)
Residents may choose a licensed hospice

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Keep all prescription drugs locked
Do not repackage or relabel medications
Keep a medication list and a medication administration record
Send medications with the resident on discharge or destroy them with consent
Telephone orders go to a licensed nurse only and are signed within 14 days

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Default is self-administration; staff may only remind, hand over, open containers or physically assist impaired residents
Staff may not fill pill organizers
Facility administration is limited to an RN, an LPN with an approved medication course (acting at RN/physician direction), a physician or another person authorized by law, on a prescriber's order
The authorized person stays on duty long enough to observe acceptance and reaction
Staff assisting with medication must read, write and understand English

policies.title: Nursing Services, Skilled Nursing Limits and Dressings
state_specifics: Facilities providing skilled nursing beyond special diets, dressings or medication need an RN (employed or contracted) for onsite supervision and a licensed nurse on call
Dressings: write down which dressings are managed, have written procedures, use authorized individuals only
Evaluate each resident receiving dressings or skilled care at least every 7 days for transfer
Orders signed within 14 days; a nurse coordinates care
Enteral feedings: written types, weight documentation and a dietitian

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: On a significant adverse change: immediate intervention, notation in the record, information to the treating party
Notify the sponsor; reasonable effort within 12 hours
Reassess and update services and equipment promptly
Use written transfer agreements with facilities that can meet needs
Send current medication list and face sheet with the resident

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care (Special Care Unit)
state_specifics: Written SCU policy given before admission with: (a) mission/philosophy, (b) admission criteria, (c) transfer and discharge criteria, (d) weekly staffing plan and added supervision, (e) activities
Also (f) cost of services, (g) staff training and CE, (h) assessment and service process, (i) behavioral health, (j) physical environment, (k) family involvement, (l) added services
Secured SCU placement needs a licensed professional's determination and updated agreement, never diagnosis alone
Secured units are individualized, reviewed at each reassessment and code compliant
Training: 2 hrs initial within 14 days and 4 hrs CE yearly (4 and 8 if both groups served); psychologist or physician on staff or consulting

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: Falls risk is part of the initial assessment
A fall or change in function triggers reassessment and service plan update
Record each fall in the incident log with time, place, date, description and action
Notify the sponsor and physician as the change-of-condition policy requires

policies.title: Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain residents with stage III/IV pressure ulcers (hospice excepted)
Assess skin on admission and at each reassessment
Dressings follow the written dressing procedures with 7-day evaluation
Report new skin breakdown as a change in condition

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: Residents may choose a licensed hospice
Hospice residents are an exception to the skilled-nursing retention bar
Extended-care re-determination for hospice residents is every 15 days
Coordinate the service plan with hospice and home health; document services provided by third parties

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Notify sponsor and physician promptly and document in the record
Final accounting of resident funds and refund per the agreement
Release or destroy medications per the medication policy with consent
A death from fire or smoke inhalation is reported within 24 hours to the State Fire Marshal and ODH

policies.title: Controlled Substance Security and Theft Prevention
state_specifics: Comply with state and federal controlled-substance law
Written policies and procedures to prevent misappropriation or theft of controlled substances
Count log and two-person reconciliation are facility-chosen controls, not rule requirements
Report suspected diversion per the abuse and incident policies
Confirm the paragraph letter in the full OAC 3701-16-09 text

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Residents have the right to freedom from abuse and financial exploitation
Staff with disqualifying offenses or registry abuse/neglect/misappropriation findings are not hired for direct care
Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to county adult protective services, law enforcement and ODH as Ohio law requires (reporting statute not verified here; have counsel confirm)
No reprisal against residents or staff who report; investigate every allegation

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Investigate and document each incident
Keep an incident log separate from the resident record, accessible to the director
Log shows time, place and date, general description, and care provided or action taken
Also note the incident in the resident's record

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Written procedures for locating missing residents, including notifying local law enforcement
Part of the disaster preparedness plan
Elopement risk is assessed on admission; secured units follow the special care unit rules
Log each event as an incident

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Physical, chemical and isolation restraints are forbidden, including locked room doors and geriatric chairs
Secured special care units are allowed only if individualized, reviewed at each reassessment, code compliant and not based solely on diagnosis
Do not admit or retain residents who need restraints
Staff are trained on the prohibition and on alternatives

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Written plan readily available on site and also kept electronically for off-site access
Evacuation: provisions for impaired mobility and transport to predetermined receiving facilities
Fire plan with fire watch and prompt notice to the local fire authority and State Fire Marshal when detection, alarm or sprinkler systems are impaired
Severe weather procedures with designated tornado shelter areas; procedures for nearby hazards (airports, chemical plants, railroads) as appropriate
Notify the ODH director by email or phone when business services are interrupted by an emergency

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: 12 fire drills a year (one per shift every 3 months); each staff member participates in one a year; residents evacuated in 2 drills per shift yearly
2 disaster drills yearly, one a tornado drill March-July; investigate and correct problems; keep written records and evaluation 3 years
Post a wall-specific floor plan on each section or floor (room use, alarms, routes, exits, extinguishers, evacuation flow)
Fire and evacuation training within 3 working days of hire (no staff alone with residents before it); annual fire prevention training for all shifts
Train residents in fire, tornado and disaster actions; monthly fire safety inspection kept 3 years

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written program of policies to assure a safe, sanitary environment, monitor compliance, investigate infections and train all staff
Designate infection prevention designee(s); submit name and email to ODH's electronic system within 10 days of appointment or change
TB control plan meeting OAC 3701-15-03 standards
Written surveillance plan using nationally recognized criteria (e.g., McGeer) with a data collection tool and use of data
Isolation, hand hygiene, laundry rules and a legionella water management program

policies.title: Smoking, Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Smoking and vaping only in designated areas
No smoking or flame where oxygen is stored or used; post 'No smoking' signs
Reasonable precautions for smoking residents; non-combustible ash receptacles; shelter in bad weather
Written pet protocol developed after consulting a veterinarian
Visitor access policy honors waiver residents' control of visitors and schedule

policies.title: Fire Reporting and Transfer Agreements
state_specifics: Report any fire, fire damage, or illness, injury or death from fire or smoke inhalation within 24 hours to the State Fire Marshal and ODH, on their forms
Written transfer agreements with facilities that can meet the needs of residents whose health or safety is or may be adversely affected by facility conditions
Review agreements annually and keep copies on file

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Specify meals offered (0-3 daily) in the agreement
No more than 16 hours between supper and breakfast; evening snack offered
Menus planned a week ahead and kept 3 months; a week of staples and 2 days of perishables on hand
Drinking water always available
A dietitian supervises therapeutic diets; staff are dietitian-trained first

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Provide or arrange varied activities
Offer a daily newspaper or community brochures
Provide community activity and transportation information
Activity planners are trained for cognitive impairment and mental illness populations

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Maintenance and Building Environment
state_specifics: Specify laundry services in the resident agreement
Maintain certificate of occupancy, plumbing code compliance and thermostatic mixing devices on bathing fixtures
Hot water 105-120 F where facility controlled
Resident-activated call system in rooms and bathrooms; one toilet, sink and tub or shower per 8 residents
New units: 100 sq ft single, 80 sq ft per person shared, max 4 per room

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Provide residents with community transportation information
Evacuation plan includes transport to receiving facilities
If the facility transports residents, drivers are licensed and vehicles insured (facility standard)

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
state_specifics: At least one qualified personal care staff member on duty at all times; overnight on-call only if call system rules in OAC 3701-16-14(B)(5) are met
When only one person is on duty, designate another qualified staff member on call
Enough staff for assessed needs, dietary, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and activities; no fixed ratio in the rules
Staff needed for the evacuation plan are present at all times; a first-aid-trained personal care staff member is on site at all times
Keep personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: No direct-care employment with a disqualifying offense under ORC 3721.121(C)(1)
No employment if forms or fingerprints under ORC 3721.121(B)(2) are not provided
No employment with an abuse, neglect or misappropriation finding on the Ohio or another state's nurse aide registry
No employment with a license action for abuse, neglect or misappropriation
ORC 3721.121 text not verified here; read before finalizing procedures

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Orientation within 3 working days: layout, job duties, policies, securing emergency help, resident rights; no time alone with residents until orientation and fire training are done
First-aid training within 60 days; personal care competency (RN/LPN-taught, ODH-approved aide program or home health aide training) before unsupervised work
Annual rights training on ORC 3721.13(A) and on comparable service for residents with similar needs
8 hours CE yearly; special population training 2 hrs initial within 14 days and 4 hrs yearly; dietitian training before therapeutic diets
Personal care staff 16+ (under 18 need on-site adult supervision)

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: No work during the communicable stage of a transmissible disease unless duties and precautions minimize transmission
No work while impaired by alcohol or drugs
Health exam by a health professional within 30 days before or on the first day; retain copies
TB screening follows the facility TB control plan under OAC 3701-15-03 (content not verified here)

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms
Each file holds health exam, first-aid certificate, orientation sign-off, background check result, CE and credentials
Track CE hours and anniversary dates for each worker
Professionals' Ohio licenses are verified and current

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff may not coerce residents to assign assets
Staff may not serve as guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related
Residents may not be used as staff
No work while impaired
Prohibit gifts, loans and financial dealings with residents (facility standard)

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications and Continuing Education
state_specifics: Administrator is 21+

Qualifies by nursing home administrator license, 3,000 hours of operational responsibility, 100 credit hours in gerontology or health care, a bachelor's degree, or a licensed health professional credential
9 hours of continuing education yearly
At least 20 hours per week on site between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.; keep an hours log

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Record holds assessments, reassessments, service plan, medication list and administration record, incident notations and signed acknowledgments
Records are confidential under ORC 3721.13(A)
Menus are kept 3 months; drill, fire inspection and monthly fire safety records are kept 3 years
Resident record retention period not verified here; confirm with counsel before setting it

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Infection prevention designee name and email to ODH within 10 days of appointment or change
Notify the ODH director when normal business services are interrupted by an emergency
Fire-related reports to the State Fire Marshal and ODH within 24 hours
Change-of-operator application at least 60 days ahead; closure notice 90 days where practicable, no less than 60
License renewal application and fee, and personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms

documents.form_number: No form number found. File is dated 04/30/2026 and listed as April 2026.
documents.issuer: Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Regulatory Operations (Licensure Unit)
documents.how_used: I located this packet on ODH's Applications and Forms page but could not open the PDF. No items are taken from it. Check it by hand for any policy checklist. The linked page is https://odh.ohio.gov/wps/portal/gov/odh/know-our-programs/residential-care-facilities-assisted-living/resources/rcfinitallicensepacket

required_items.text: Resident agreement: an explanation of all charges to the resident, including security deposits if applicable.
Resident agreement: a statement that all charges, fines or penalties assessed against the resident are included in the agreement.
Resident agreement: a statement that the basic rate will not change without 30 days' written notice to the resident or, if the resident cannot understand it, to the sponsor.
Resident agreement: an explanation of the facility's policy for refunding charges on absence, discharge or transfer, and its policy for refunding security deposits.

Resident agreement: an explanation of the services offered, the types of skilled nursing care the facility provides or allows, the authorized providers, and the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care.
Resident agreement: an explanation of the extent and types of services the facility will provide and who is responsible for payment.
Resident agreement: a statement that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified in (E)(5).
Policy to give residents before admission: the residents' rights policy and procedures required by ORC 3721.12.
Policy to give residents before admission: the facility's smoking policy. Rule -07 cites 3701-16-13(W), but smoking appears at 3701-16-13(U) in the current rule text.

Policy to give residents before admission: policies on advance directives and DNR orders, with an explanation of the resident's rights under state law. An advance directive or DNR order cannot be required as a condition of admission.
Information to give residents before admission: the definition of skilled nursing care from rule 3701-16-01.
For residents seeking a special care unit, the facility's policy on care in that unit. It must contain the items F(5)(a) to F(5)(l) below.
Special care unit policy: a statement of mission or philosophy that reflects the needs of the special population.
Special care unit policy: admission criteria, including screening criteria if applicable.
Special care unit policy: transfer and discharge criteria and procedures.

Special care unit policy: a weekly staffing plan if applicable. It must state how the plan differs from the rest of the facility (F(5)(d)(i)) and the necessary increase in supervision for residents with cognitive impairments or serious mental illness (F(5)(d)(ii)).
Special care unit policy: a description of activities offered (frequency and type), how they meet the unit residents' needs, and how they differ from the rest of the facility if applicable.
Special care unit policy: a listing of the costs of services the facility provides to the resident.
Special care unit policy: specialized staff training and continuing education practices.
Special care unit policy: the process for assessment and provision of services, including how services change as the resident's condition changes.
Special care unit policy: if necessary, how the facility addresses residents' behavioral healthcare needs.
Special care unit policy: the physical environment and design features that support residents' functioning.
Special care unit policy: family involvement and the availability of family support programs.
Special care unit policy: any services or procedures over and above those in the rest of the facility, if applicable.
An explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabled or potentially disabled residents, and its policy on transferring residents to units that accommodate disabilities.
Any other facility policies that residents must follow.

If the facility has a policy of entering into risk agreements: a written explanation of the policy and of the provisions a risk agreement may contain. It must be given to each prospective resident or sponsor, with a signed acknowledgment kept on file.

A written disaster preparedness plan to be followed in an emergency or disaster. It must be readily available in the facility and also kept electronically for off-site access. It must include J(1) to J(6) below.

Disaster plan: procedures for evacuating all individuals, including (a) provisions for residents with impaired mobility and (b) provisions for transporting all residents to a predetermined appropriate facility or facilities.

Disaster plan: a plan for protecting all persons in a fire and procedures for fire control and evacuation. This includes a fire watch and prompt notice to the local fire authority and state fire marshal when fire detection, alarm or sprinkler systems are impaired or inoperable.
Disaster plan: procedures for locating missing residents, including notifying local law enforcement.
Disaster plan: procedures for residents' health and safety in severe weather such as tornadoes and floods, and designation of tornado shelter areas.
Disaster plan: procedures, as appropriate, for facilities near areas with specific disaster potential (airports, chemical plants, railroad tracks).
Disaster plan: notification of the director by email or phone when normal business services are interrupted by an emergency or disaster involving the facility.

Drills and records: required fire exit drills and disaster preparedness drills (including a tornado drill). The facility must investigate and correct problems found. It must keep a written drill record and evaluation for three years.
Post in each section or floor a wall-specific floor plan showing room use, alarm sending stations, evacuation routes and exits, fire alarms and extinguishers, and flow of resident evacuation.
Train all staff in fire control and evacuation procedures within three working days of hire. A staff member may not be alone with residents before this training.
Annual fire prevention training for regularly scheduled staff on all shifts, with records kept.
Train all residents in the proper actions to take in a fire, tornado, disaster or other emergency.

Smoking: permitted only in designated areas. Oxygen areas are smoke-free and need 'No smoking' signs. The facility must take reasonable precautions for residents who smoke, and for outdoor smoking in bad weather. This is the content behind the smoking policy in 3701-16-07(F)(2).
Report any fire, fire damage, or illness, injury or death from fire or smoke inhalation within 24 hours to the State Fire Marshal and ODH.

Written transfer agreements with other facilities that can meet the needs of residents who must be transferred because their health or safety is, or may be, adversely affected by conditions in the facility.

Incident handling: investigate and document each incident, and keep an incident log separate from the resident record. The log must be accessible to the director and show the time, place and date, a general description, and the care provided or action taken. Also make a notation in the resident's record. This rule item is a requirement that the policies must address, not a policy by itself.

Written policies and procedures to assure a safe, sanitary and comfortable environment and to control the development and transmission of infections and diseases. These sit within an infection prevention and control program that monitors compliance with them, investigates and controls infections, and trains all staff.

Infection control program: designate one or more infection prevention and control designees. Submit their name and contact information (including email) on the ODH-prescribed electronic system within 10 days of appointment. Only part of this item was visible to me, and the designee qualifications are in sub-items such as (c).
Infection control program: a tuberculosis control plan that meets the standards in rule 3701-15-03.

Infection control program: a written surveillance plan for monitoring and tracking infections using nationally recognized criteria such as McGeer, with a data collection tool and use of the surveillance data. Later sub-items of (C)(3) and any further (C) items were not seen.

Staff orientation and training within three working days of hire, applicable to the staff member's job. It must include at least: (1) the physical layout of the facility; (2) the staff member's job responsibilities; (3) the facility's policies and procedures; (4) how to secure emergency assistance; and (5) residents' rights. The staff member may not be alone with residents until this and the fire training are done.

Annual staff training, and training as needed, to implement each resident right under ORC 3721.13(A). It must explain (1) residents' rights and the staff's responsibility in implementing them, and (2) the staff's obligation to give residents with similar needs comparable service.

Training for staff who provide personal care services: first aid within 60 days of hire; personal care training or an equivalent approved program before unsupervised care; initial and annual training for special populations (cognitive impairment, serious mental illness, and others); and eight hours of continuing education annually. Therapeutic diet staff must be dietitian-trained (F).

Hiring exclusions for direct-care positions: disqualifying offenses under ORC 3721.121(C)(1), failure to complete background check forms or fingerprints, nurse aide registry findings (Ohio or another state), and professional license discipline for abuse, neglect or misappropriation.

Personnel health policies: no work during the communicable stage of a transmissible disease unless duties and precautions minimize transmission; no work while impaired by alcohol or drugs; a pre-employment health exam within 30 days before or on the first day of work.

Resident medications: for controlled substances, the facility must comply with state and federal law and have policies and procedures in place to prevent misappropriation or theft of controlled substances. The paragraph letter was not visible in the excerpt, so confirm it in the full rule.

required_items.text: Closure notice to the director must include (1) an address where the operator can be reached, (2) a plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and (3) assurances that residents go to the most integrated and appropriate setting, taking account of their needs, choice and best interests. Notice is due at least 90 days ahead where practicable, and no less than 60 days ahead.

official.notes: I found no single ODH policy checklist, plan of operation or policy-review form for Ohio RCFs, so the items above come from the OAC Chapter 3701-16 sections that require written policies, plans or resident-facing documents. Ohio's initial application under OAC 3701-16-03(A) asks for administrative items only: zoning, financial solvency, ownership, floor plan, certificate of occupancy, fire and heating inspection reports, and the fee. These are excluded. ODH does not appear to review a policy manual at licensure. Compliance with the policy items is evaluated during on-site surveys, which ODH says include at least one unannounced survey in each 9- to 15-month cycle. So the manual should be organised so surveyors can find each policy by rule. Matching the order of the rules is a sensible approach, but it is not an ODH requirement. Limits of this review: (1) I could not open the April 2026 Initial License Packet or the Initial Application Instructions PDFs, so check them for any additional policy items. (2) OAC 3701-16-12 and 3701-16-09 were read only through search excerpts, and the other items in those rules were not seen. (3) I did not review other 3701-16 rules or ORC 3721.12/3721.13 (residents' rights policy and procedures, which -07(F)(1) requires), or the Assisted Living Waiver provider requirements (ODA/ODM). These rules likely contain more written-policy items, such as resident assessments, activities, dietary and therapeutic diets, records, and abuse reporting. (4) Rule -07(F)(2) cites the smoking policy at 3701-16-13(W), but the current 3701-16-13 places smoking at (U). Use (U) and confirm with ODH at liccert@odh.ohio.gov or (614) 466-7713. (5) Item IDs are the rule paragraph numbers; the same letter (for example E, K or L) appears in different rules and is distinguished by the cite. (6) Item text is condensed from the rules, not verbatim.
